1.text: Day 1: the AI runs the winter with manual evoA-h001 (0 pages)
Night 0: before learning from any failure, the coach writes its best manual from general knowledge (the baseline every learning night must beat)

There are no failures yet. The current manual is purely reactive: there is no forecast, no trend gauge and no habits. The AI is woken only once reserves are already thin, gas facilities are unprotected, and nothing ensures prompt, gradual restoration. Hard storms typically fail through late preparation, supply collapse after gas freeze-offs, frequency excursions and slow restoration.
Idea [habit]: Forecast-led preparation, anticipatory shedding, protected gas, prompt restore (expects -30% homes dark, +1 storms)
Tested 'Forecast-led preparation, anticipatory shedding, protected gas, prompt restore' on 9 storm runs: ✗✗✗✗✗✗✓✓✓ (-46.5% homes dark on the failed storms)
Kept: Forecast-led preparation, anticipatory shedding, protected gas, prompt restore (-46% homes dark on the failed storms, +0 storms)

New manual page saved to MongoDB: "Prepare early, shed ahead, restore promptly": When deep cold is forecast, line up extra plants, imports and conservation early. If supply is falling, shed a little ahead while keeping gas sites powered. Bring homes back as soon as reserves recover.

l2.insight: I underestimated new habits, overestimated authority changes, and kept proposing restoration variants the kept habit already covered.

new_proposals.title: Show the actual MW shortfall at decision time
Cap oversized outages while reserves are positive

l2.proposed_strategy:
- Before proposing, list what kept edits (forecast-led prep, tiered prompt restoration) already cover; reject your own ideas that overlap them.
- Read the failed storms for a NEW failure mode (e.g. under-preparation, wrong targeting, protected-load errors), not more 'restore excess cuts' variants.
- Predict relative to remaining headroom: after big wins, gains on leftover dark hours are small; but a first fix to an untouched mode can exceed -40%.
- Treat authority or control-shift edits as high-risk: predict near zero or positive unless the storms show the habit is right and only blocked.
- Use the passed storm to check each edit would not break what already works; drop edits that would change its behavior.
- Prefer one concrete habit or briefing change per idea, stating the exact storm pattern it fixes and why its size is plausible.

l2.insight: My predictions are now accurate, but I keep proposing small restore tweaks of about -13% that cannot clear the keep bar. I need bigger, new-mode fixes.

new_proposals.title: Habits and control room size the cuts
Anticipate falls with trend-sized cuts, not blocks
Show the AI its own lessons and recent swings

l2.proposed_strategy:
- First list what the kept edits (forecast-led prep, tiered prompt restoration) already cover. Drop any idea that is mainly another restore-excess-cuts or reserve-band restore variant: these keep measuring about -13%, which is rejected as insufficient.
- In the failed storms, find the largest remaining source of homes x hours dark, such as wrong feeder targeting, protected-load mistakes or slow early shedding. Aim one idea at it with a clear path to beating -20%.
- Calibrate predictions to past measurements: restore and band tweaks about -12%, cold-weather commitment and precommit edits near 0. Authority shifts range from about -8% to +10%, so predict about -5% to +5% unless the storms clearly show the habit is right but blocked.
- When single ideas are each too small, propose one combined habit edit that bundles two complementary fixes from different modes. Predict it as less than the sum of its parts.
- Use the passed storm to drop any edit that would change behavior that already works. State the exact storm pattern each idea fixes and the mechanism behind its predicted size.
- Rank ideas by expected size. Only propose an idea predicted at -15% or better when you have specific evidence for it, and never inflate a prediction to clear the bar.

l2.insight: My predictions became accurate, but I kept proposing small, safe tweaks of about -10% that never cleared the bar. I need fewer, bolder, combined edits.

new_proposals.title: Hard limit: hand back surplus cuts each hour
Brief the AI on surplus cuts, not distant cold
Mid-band prompt restoration in bigger steps

l2.proposed_strategy:
- Recent edits landing near -10 to -13% are all rejected as insufficient, so aim each idea at clearing roughly -15% or more; drop ideas you honestly predict smaller.
- Merge complementary small wins into one coherent edit, e.g. mid-band restore plus a cap on oversized cuts plus forecast-blind cut sizing, and predict the combined effect with a modest overlap discount.
- Look in the failed storms for the largest remaining block of dark homes x hours (duration, scale or targeting) and attack that directly rather than tuning margins.
- Skip authority-shift and resource-saving edits unless the storms show a large, specific blockage; they have given about 0 to -8%.
- Keep predictions calibrated: anchor on measured results of similar past edits, check the passed storm for breakage, and state the exact pattern fixed and why the size is plausible.
- Do not repeat rejected ideas or overlap kept edits (forecast-led prep, tiered prompt restoration).

l2.insight: I kept predicting big gains from cut-sizing and authority edits that overlapped kept habits; actual results were near zero or worse.

new_proposals.title: Surface the lessons on what a cut number means
Gauge showing homes that could come back now

l2.proposed_strategy:
- The kept habit edit (mid-band restore, no anticipatory over-cuts) already captured cut-sizing gains. Any new cap, cushion or return-excess edit overlaps it, so predict near 0% unless the storms show a different pattern.
- Never propose authority shifts. They measured +0.5%, -7.9%, -2.8% and +15.8%, and moving cut or restore control away from the AI can backfire badly.
- Look in the failed storms for dark homes x hours that persist after the kept habits: long-duration outages, poorly targeted cuts, slow restoration after the crunch, unused resources. Attack one such new mechanism per idea.
- Calibrate before claiming a big effect. Start from the measured result of the most similar past edit, halve it if it touches a kept edit's territory, and only claim -15% or more when the cited storm pattern supports it.
- Use the passed storm to check each idea for breakage. If an idea could add cuts or delay restores there, predict a positive (worse) effect or drop it.
- Don't merge ideas into one combined edit; past merges measured about half of what was predicted. Don't repeat rejected ideas or overlap kept ones (forecast-led prep, tiered restoration, mid-band restore habit).

l2.insight: After the kept habit, I kept predicting small gains from cut and restore tweaks that actually made things worse. I ignored interference and anchored on optimism.

new_proposals.title: Hold warm units committed through deep cold
Show the real megawatt gap in briefing

l2.proposed_strategy:
- Default prediction is 0% to +3%. Since the kept mid-band restore habit, every edit measured between -3.2% and +7.4%. Only predict below -5% when a failed storm shows a dark-hours pattern the kept habit cannot reach, and name that storm.
- Treat any edit that changes cut sizing, cut caps, damping, battery refill timing or restore triggers as interfering with the kept habit. Predict it as positive (worse), from +2% to +8%, or don't propose it. Night 11's damping and refill edits measured +7.4% and +2.6%.
- Never propose authority shifts or hard-limit caps or cushions. Their history is +15.8%, +7.4% and +0.1%. Gauge alarms and briefing tweaks measure about -3%, so predict -2% to -3% for those, never more.
- Look for mechanisms outside the cut and restore loop: which homes are targeted (critical loads, rotation fairness), cold-start or crew delays after the crunch, and supply-side switching. Cite the exact storm hours where homes stayed dark.
- For each idea, walk through the passed storm hour by hour. If the idea fires there at all, add +2% to the prediction. Report a range and pick its upper (worse) end as the point estimate.
- Propose fewer ideas, each a single new mechanism. Prefer one well-calibrated near-zero prediction over a hopeful big claim, because prediction error matters as much as finding a keeper.

l2.insight: I kept forecasting gains for habit and limit edits that measured worse, and underrated briefing edits, the only type that reliably helped.

new_proposals.title: Briefing: show restorable cut and recent shed swings
Alarm: homes dark while cushion has returned

l2.proposed_strategy:
- Calibrate by edit type from measured history since the kept restore habit. Briefing and memory edits measured -3.0% and -5.2%, gauge alarms -1.8% to -2.9%, and habit or hard-limit edits from -3.2% to +7.5%.
- Spend most proposals on briefing_memory. Showing the AI its excess cut is the most reliable lever (-7.3% before the habit, -5.2% after). Predict -4% to -6% and make each version sharper: cut size vs. gap, the last 3 hours of outcomes, and no stale forecasts.
- Gauge alarms: propose them only when tied to a named storm hour where homes stayed dark during recovery. Predict -2% to -3%.
- Do not propose habits, hard limits, authority shifts, cold-prep or battery timing. Every one since night 9 measured worse, and our negative predictions got the sign wrong. If one is unavoidable, predict +3% to +8%.
- Before predicting, check that the idea is not a near-duplicate of a rejected edit. If it builds on a prior briefing, predict about 1 pt better than that briefing's measured result, never more than 2 pts better.
- Use the passed storm only as a veto. If the idea would change decisions there, drop it rather than adjusting the number. Give a point estimate at the midpoint of the type's historical range.

l2.insight: I broke my own ban, proposing hard limits and habits with negative predictions. Every one measured positive. Only cut-sizing briefings reliably helped.

new_proposals.title: Briefing: per-hour excess cut MW and true trend
Wake the AI only when homes can clearly return

l2.proposed_strategy:
- Predict from category base rates, not hopes. Briefing edits that show the AI its excess cut or teach cut sizing measured -2.7% to -5.2%, so predict -3% to -4%. Other briefing tweaks measured about -3% to +0.8%, so predict -1%.
- Hard limits measured 0.1%, 3.6%, 7.4% and 0.4%, and habits measured 2.6%, 3.2% and 7.5%. Do not propose either. If you must, predict +3% or worse. Never predict a negative number for these.
- Gauge alarms split: -2.9% when about restoring, +1.8% when tied to outages. Predict 0% unless the alarm only fires when restoring is clearly possible.
- Build on the best result (night 13, -5.2%, briefing on excess cut and cut sizing). Make it sharper in one way, such as per-hour excess megawatts or naming storm hours where homes stayed dark needlessly. Cite those hours.
- Before submitting, check the sign. If the edit adds a constraint, a threshold or a timing rule to the cut and restore loop, it measures positive (worse). Only information-only briefing changes have reliably measured negative.
- Propose at most 2 ideas: one sharpened cut-sizing briefing predicted at -4%, and optionally one new information-only idea predicted at -1% to -2%.

l2.proposed_strategy:
- Default to physical build edits (winterizing, fuel and gas supply, hardening); they have been kept and predicted within ~4 pts.
- Before proposing any habit, briefing or authority change that makes shedding earlier or larger, check it against the passed contrast storm. If it would cut power on a calm or healthy-margin day, drop it.
- For every rule-based edit, first estimate the calm-day cost, then the storm benefit. Predict the net. If the net could be positive, predict a positive number or skip the edit.
- Never add triggers that fire on pass-line or near-threshold margins (reserve drain, near-zero restore bans). They read as gaming.
- Shrink predictions for small, narrow tweaks toward 0 to ±5%, since moderate-margin unwinds and deep-cold habits measured near zero. Reserve large predictions for broad builds stacked on prior builds.
- Propose 2 well-separated ideas, at least one a build. Say explicitly why each edit cannot hurt the passed storm.

l2.proposed_strategy:
- Lead with physical build edits (winterizing, fuel supply, weatherproofing wind, wells and coal) that target the failure mode named in the failed storms. Predict -10% to -15% for broad builds; builds have measured -7% to -18%.
- Make the second idea either another distinct build or an unwind of oversized outages only (the one kept rule type). Never add triggers that shed earlier or larger, and never act on near-threshold margins.
- For any rule, habit or briefing edit, predict 0% to +5% by default. Narrow tweaks have measured slightly positive (+2.8, +2.9, +5.7). Predict negative only if the failed storms show a large, specific loss it removes.
- Check each edit against the passed contrast storm and state the calm-day cost. If any shedding could fire on a healthy-margin day, drop the edit; don't just shrink its prediction.
- Size build predictions by how often the targeted failure appears in the shown storms. Widespread failures get about -15%, single-storm failures about -7%.
- Don't re-propose rejected ideas reworded (moderate-margin unwinds, deep-cold habits, reserve-drain triggers, cushions during outages).
